                    ### Question
                    Which of the following enzymes can be considered a good marker of drug-induced hemolytic anemia ?:

                    ### Options
                    opa. Aspartate aminotransferase (Aspartate transaminase, AST).
opb. Creatine kinase (CK).
opc. Glucose-6 phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PDH).
opd. Lactate dehydrogenase.

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
Glucose-6 phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PDH) deficiency can lead to drug-induced oxidative stress and hemolytic anemia, making G6PDH a good marker for drug-induced hemolytic anemia. Lactate dehydrogenase is released from damaged red blood cells during hemolysis and can also be a possible marker of hemolytic anemia, including drug-induced cases. Evidence supports the relationship between G6PDH deficiency and drug-induced hemolytic anemia.
